EXECUTIVE EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

THIS EXECUTIVE EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into as of July 1, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between Marbury Instruments, Inc., a Delaware corporation with its principal offices at 300 Wollaston Street, Boston, Massachusetts (the "Company"), and Naomi Adeyemi, an individual residing in Brookline, Massachusetts ("Executive").

1. Employment and Duties.

1.1 Position. The Company employs Executive as its Chief Financial Officer, reporting to the Chief Executive Officer. Executive shall perform the duties customary to that office and such other duties consistent with it as the Chief Executive Officer or the Board of Directors (the "Board") assigns.

1.2 Full Time and Attention. Executive shall devote her full business time, attention and best efforts to the Company. Executive may serve on the board of one non-competing for-profit company and on charitable and civic boards, and may manage personal investments, so long as those activities do not materially interfere with her duties.

1.3 Location. Executive's principal place of employment is the Company's Boston offices, subject to business travel. A relocation of that place of employment by more than fifty (50) miles constitutes Good Reason under Section 5.4.

2. Term. This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues until terminated under Section 5. Executive's employment is at will: either the Company or Executive may end it at any time, with or without Cause or Good Reason, subject to the notice and payment obligations in Section 5. No provision of this Agreement alters the at-will nature of the employment.

3. Compensation.

3.1 Base Salary. The Company shall pay Executive an annual base salary of Four Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars ($420,000), payable in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices and subject to withholding. The Board or its Compensation Committee shall review the base salary at least annually and may increase it; it may not be decreased except as part of an across-the-board reduction applying to all senior executives.

3.2 Annual Bonus. Executive is eligible for an annual cash bonus with a target of fifty percent (50%) of base salary, based on Company and individual performance objectives set by the Compensation Committee within the first ninety (90) days of each fiscal year. Any earned bonus is paid by March 15 of the following calendar year, and Executive must be employed on the payment date except as Section 5.3 provides.

3.3 Equity. Subject to Board approval, the Company shall grant Executive an option to purchase two hundred thousand (200,000) shares of common stock at an exercise price equal to the fair market value on the grant date, vesting twenty-five percent (25%) on the first anniversary of the Effective Date and in equal monthly installments over the following thirty-six (36) months, subject to the Company's equity incentive plan and the applicable award agreement.

3.4 Benefits. Executive is eligible to participate in the health, welfare, retirement, and other benefit plans the Company makes generally available to its senior executives, on the terms of those plans as they may change from time to time.

3.5 Paid Time Off. Executive is entitled to paid time off in accordance with Company policy, and to the paid sick time required by the Massachusetts Earned Sick Time Law, M.G.L. c. 149, § 148C.

3.6 Expenses. The Company shall reimburse Executive for reasonable business expenses incurred in performing her duties, in accordance with Company policy and on timely submission of documentation.

3.7 Indemnification and D&O Coverage. The Company shall indemnify Executive to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law and its certificate of incorporation and bylaws for actions taken in the course of her service, shall advance expenses subject to an undertaking to repay if indemnification is ultimately unavailable, and shall cover Executive under its directors' and officers' liability insurance on the same terms as its other senior officers, during employment and for six (6) years afterward.

4. Confidentiality, Inventions and Company Property.

4.1 Confidential Information. Executive shall not, during or after employment, use or disclose the Company's confidential information except in the performance of her duties. Confidential information does not include information that is or becomes public through no fault of Executive, that Executive lawfully knew before her employment, or that a third party discloses to her without a duty of confidence.

4.2 Defend Trade Secrets Act Notice. Under 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b), Executive shall not be held criminally or civilly liable under any federal or state trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that is made in confidence to a federal, state, or local government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney, solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law, or that is made in a complaint or other document filed under seal in a lawsuit or other proceeding.

4.3 Protected Activity. Nothing in this Agreement prohibits Executive from filing a charge with, reporting possible violations of law to, or participating in an investigation by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the National Labor Relations Board, or any other government agency, or from receiving a whistleblower award. Executive need not notify the Company before doing so.

4.4 Inventions. Executive assigns to the Company all inventions she conceives or reduces to practice during her employment that relate to the Company's business or result from work performed for the Company, and shall execute the documents reasonably necessary to perfect that assignment. This assignment does not apply to an invention Executive develops entirely on her own time without using the Company's equipment, supplies, facilities, or trade secret information, except for inventions that relate to the Company's business or actual or demonstrably anticipated research or development, or that result from work performed for the Company.

4.5 Return of Property. On termination of employment for any reason, Executive shall promptly return all Company property, including documents, devices, credentials, and all copies of confidential information in her possession.

5. Termination.

5.1 Death or Disability. Employment ends automatically on Executive's death, and the Company may end it on Executive's disability that prevents her from performing the essential functions of her position, with or without reasonable accommodation, for one hundred twenty (120) days in any twelve-month period.

5.2 Accrued Obligations. On any termination, the Company shall pay Executive her earned but unpaid base salary through the date of termination, any earned but unpaid bonus for a completed fiscal year, accrued and unused paid time off to the extent required by Massachusetts law, and unreimbursed business expenses, in each case within the time the Massachusetts Wage Act, M.G.L. c. 149, § 148, requires.

5.3 Severance. If the Company terminates Executive without Cause, or Executive resigns for Good Reason, and in either case Executive signs and does not revoke the Company's standard separation agreement and release of claims within sixty (60) days after the date of termination, the Company shall pay Executive twelve (12) months of her then-current base salary in accordance with regular payroll practices, pay a pro-rata portion of her target annual bonus for the year of termination, and pay the employer portion of COBRA premiums for up to twelve (12) months or until Executive becomes eligible for other group coverage, whichever is earlier.

5.4 Cause and Good Reason. "Cause" means Executive's conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony or a crime involving dishonesty; her willful misconduct or gross negligence that causes material harm to the Company; her material breach of this Agreement or of a written Company policy; or her willful and continued failure to perform her duties, in each case after written notice describing the conduct and, where the conduct is curable, a period of thirty (30) days to cure it. "Good Reason" means, without Executive's consent, a material diminution in her authority, duties or responsibilities; a reduction in her base salary other than an across-the-board reduction; a relocation described in Section 1.3; or a material breach of this Agreement by the Company, in each case where Executive gives written notice within ninety (90) days after the event, the Company fails to cure within thirty (30) days, and Executive resigns within thirty (30) days after the cure period ends.

5.5 Section 409A. The payments under this Agreement are intended to be exempt from or compliant with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code and shall be construed accordingly. Each installment is a separate payment. If Executive is a "specified employee" within the meaning of Section 409A on the date of termination, any payment of deferred compensation that would otherwise be made in the six (6) months after separation from service shall instead be made on the first business day of the seventh month. Reimbursements are made by the end of the year following the year the expense is incurred, and the amount available in one year does not affect the amount available in another.

5.6 Section 280G. If any payment would be subject to the excise tax under Section 4999 of the Internal Revenue Code, the payments shall be reduced to the largest amount that would not trigger the excise tax, but only if that reduction leaves Executive better off on an after-tax basis than receiving the full amount.

5.7 Resignation from Offices. On termination for any reason, Executive resigns from all offices and directorships she holds with the Company and its affiliates, and shall execute any document confirming that resignation.

6. Restrictive Covenants.

6.1 Non-Solicitation of Employees. For twelve (12) months after the end of her employment, Executive shall not solicit any person who was employed by the Company during her last six (6) months of employment to leave the Company. A general advertisement not targeted at Company employees, and the hiring of a person who responds to one, do not violate this Section.

6.2 Non-Solicitation of Customers. For twelve (12) months after the end of her employment, Executive shall not solicit any customer of the Company with whom she had material contact during her last twelve (12) months of employment, for the purpose of providing products or services competitive with those the Company provided to that customer.

6.3 Non-Competition. For twelve (12) months after the end of her employment, Executive shall not provide services substantially similar to those she provided the Company to any business that competes with the Company in the design or manufacture of precision measurement instruments, in any geographic area in which she provided services or had a material presence in the last two (2) years of her employment. This Section 6.3 is entered into in compliance with the Massachusetts Noncompetition Agreement Act, M.G.L. c. 149, § 24L: it is supported by garden leave, under which the Company shall pay Executive fifty percent (50%) of her highest annualized base salary within the two years preceding termination for the duration of the restricted period; it does not apply if the Company terminates Executive without Cause or lays her off; Executive was given this Agreement with the formal offer and at least ten (10) business days before the Effective Date; and Executive is advised of her right to consult counsel before signing.

6.4 Reasonableness. Executive acknowledges that these covenants are reasonable in scope, duration and geography, are necessary to protect the Company's trade secrets, confidential information and goodwill, and do not prevent her from earning a living. If a court finds a covenant overbroad, it shall be modified to the extent necessary to make it enforceable rather than struck.

6.5 Notice to Future Employers. Executive shall inform any prospective employer of these covenants before accepting employment during the restricted period, and the Company may notify a future employer of them.

7. Dispute Resolution. Any dispute arising out of this Agreement or Executive's employment shall be resolved in the state or federal courts located in Suffolk County, Massachusetts, and each party consents to jurisdiction and venue there. Nothing in this Section limits either party's right to seek injunctive relief to enforce Section 4 or Section 6, or Executive's right to file an administrative charge under Section 4.3.

8. General.

8.1 Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules, except that Section 6.3 is governed by Massachusetts law in all events.

8.2 Assignment. The Company may assign this Agreement to a successor in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets. Executive may not assign it, other than by will or the laws of descent.

8.3 Entire Agreement; Amendment. This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties about Executive's employment and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings about it, including any offer letter. It may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both parties, and no failure to enforce a provision is a waiver of it.

8.4 Severability. If any provision is held unenforceable, it shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary and the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect.

8.5 Withholding. All payments are subject to applicable tax withholding.

8.6 Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
